c.tagline: Sint Maarten's boardwalk capital — duty-free Front Street, Great Bay sands, and cruise-ship bustle on the Dutch side.

taxi.fareNote: No Uber or ride-hailing. Taxis use government-set fixed fares by zone (quoted per two passengers, with surcharges after 10 PM and for extra luggage); agree the price before you get in. U.S. dollars are fine.

emergency.note: On the Dutch side dial 911 for police, 912 for ambulance, and 919 for fire. The Netherlands Antillean guilder is the currency, but U.S. dollars are accepted everywhere.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch belongings on Front Street on busy cruise days and skip the quieter Back Street area late at night; never leave valuables on beaches or in rental cars.

hood_desc: The capital's walkable core on Great Bay — the duty-free shops of Front Street, the historic courthouse on Wathey Square, and the beachfront Boardwalk lined with open-air restaurants, casinos, and bars; the heart of the cruise-day bustle.
A resort-lined bay on the peninsula just west of town, with a calm beach, big beachfront hotels, and a golf course; an easy walk or short drive from Philipsburg yet quieter than Front Street.
A dense strip around the lagoon and yacht marina near the airport, packed with the island's best restaurants, casinos, and late-night bars; convenient and lively, popular with boaters and night owls.
The beach zone at the end of the runway, famous for Maho Beach plane-spotting, plus Mullet Bay's white sands and big resort-casinos; energetic and firmly beach-and-party focused.
A calmer, sunrise-facing stretch of the east coast, with upscale resorts, the Oyster Pond marina, and reef snorkeling off Dawn Beach; secluded and relaxed, away from the crowds.
lodging: Sonesta Maho Beach Resort Casino & Spa

water.note: Desalinated tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Minibuses run mostly in daylight (around 6 AM to 7 PM); the cruise-pier water taxi runs during ship hours. Taxis fill the gaps at night.
transit.note: Sint Maarten has no rail. Visitors get around by shared minibus vans, taxis, or rental car, plus a water taxi linking the cruise pier to Philipsburg's Boardwalk. The island is small, so cross-border trips to the French side take under 30 minutes.
transit.pay: Shared minibus vans charge about $1-2 (or the guilder equivalent), paid in cash to the driver — wave one down along the road. The cruise-pier water taxi to the Boardwalk runs on a paid day-pass. Taxis use fixed government-set fares.

bus: Public minibuses (shared vans) to Simpson Bay, Marigot, and across the island
ferry: Water taxi from the cruise pier to the Boardwalk / Great Bay
Ferries to Saba and St. Eustatius (Statia)

transit.m: Taxi from SXM to Philipsburg (15-20 min)
Public minibus toward Philipsburg via Simpson Bay (infrequent)

tip.r: Many restaurants add a 10-15% service charge; if not, 15-18% is customary. U.S. dollars are accepted everywhere alongside the guilder.
